steps.label: Ordered what moved first, 100–120 s
steps.summary: first to move: vehicle.velocity[x] at 100.13 s, propulsion.throttle at 105.397 s, actuator.output[ch[2]] at 105.447 s

result.headline: Throttle command dropped to zero at 113.146 s with no recorded event; altitude then fell from 50 m to 19 m.
result.explanation: A control fault occurred in the propulsion loop (throttle and ch[2]) at about 113.1 s. The recording shows no mode change or failsafe and does not show who commanded zero throttle. Roll and yaw were already disturbed before it.

evidence.quote: SHIFT propulsion.throttle changed level for good at t=113.146 s: median 39.5 before, 0 after % (11.3x its variation before)
evidence.shows: The throttle command went to 0 and stayed there. Nothing in the data explains why.

evidence.quote: SHIFT actuator.output[ch[2]] changed level for good at t=113.091 s: median 1420 before, 1100 after us (10x its variation before)
evidence.shows: The motor output went to minimum pulse width, 0.055 s before the throttle shift is logged. The output follows the command, so it is not a stuck output.

evidence.quote: ROLE actuator.output[ch[2]] follows propulsion.throttle (correlation 0.995 over the recording): it serves that loop
evidence.shows: ch[2] is the propulsion channel. The fault is at or upstream of the throttle command, not in the output stage.

evidence.quote: SHIFT vehicle.altitude[relative] changed level for good at t=117.513 s: median 49.873 before, 18.974 after m (25.7x its variation before)
evidence.shows: Altitude was lost after the throttle cut, so it is a consequence.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=1.057 s controller.event[mavros: Battery] mavros: Battery: WARN: Low voltage
evidence.shows: The only event in the recording is a low-voltage warning at start-up. It is a battery lead, not shown to be linked to the cut.

checked.check: Listed all events in the recording
checked.result: One event only: the battery low-voltage warning at 1.057 s. No mode change or failsafe is recorded anywhere in the flight.

checked.check: Sequence of signals leaving baseline from 100 s to 120 s
checked.result: Throttle left baseline at 105.397 s, then yaw and roll setpoints at 108.872 and 109.405 s. Outputs ch[3] to ch[5] moved at 112.799 s, and altitude left baseline last at 116.997 s.
checked.about: Control instability before the cut, with the altitude loss as an effect

checked.result: ch[2] went from 1476 to 1100 us and throttle from 47 to 0. Roll tracking error doubled (3.005 to 6.137 deg). Pitch and yaw tracking did not worsen.
checked.about: Propulsion loop is where the fault sits

checked.result: Velocity x and y changed, but the 5 s medians return to normal flight values. Setpoints moved at the same time, so it looks like a manoeuvre rather than a fault.
No earlier cases in the workspace.

effects.quote: SHIFT vehicle.altitude[relative] changed level for good at t=117.513 s: median 49.873 before, 18.974 after m (25.7x its variation before)
effects.why: Altitude fell after the throttle went to zero.

effects.quote: CONSTANT propulsion.throttle was varying, then held 0 from t=114.187 s to the end of the recording (15.879 s, 39 samples)
effects.why: This is the throttle staying at zero after the cut.

effects.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[2]] was varying, then held 1100 from t=114.687 s to the end of the recording (15.643 s, 46 samples)
effects.why: This is the motor output staying at minimum and following the throttle command.

next_action.action: Pull the autopilot's own log for the end of the flight: mode, failsafe, battery and ESC data.
next_action.why: Separates a commanded cut (mode or failsafe) from a battery or power loss and from a motor or ESC fault. This recording holds none of those signals.
how: Export flight-controller log messages and mode changes from 105 s to 120 s.
Export battery voltage and current and the motor/ESC telemetry for the same window.
Compare battery voltage with the 1.057 s low-voltage warning.
next_action.baseline: Throttle and ch[2] behaviour in this recording before 105 s, plus any normal flight of UAV-06 on the same battery.

outcomes.label: Failsafe or mode change at cut time
outcomes.means: The cut was commanded by the autopilot or an operator, so the cause lies in why it triggered.
outcomes.then: Trace the trigger through the control and battery signals.

outcomes.label: Battery voltage sagged just before cut
outcomes.means: A power or battery cutoff is leading, and the start-up warning matters.
outcomes.then: Request the discharge history and a battery inspection.

outcomes.label: No command change, ESC or motor lost
outcomes.means: The fault is in the propulsion hardware.
outcomes.then: Plan a bench test of the ESC and motor.

unknowns: Who or what commanded throttle to 0 at 113.146 s. The recording has no mode, failsafe or operator signal.
Battery voltage and current are not recorded, so the low-voltage warning cannot be tied to the cut.
Whether the pre-cut roll and yaw swings came before the cut because they caused it or because they share its cause.

data_requests.what: Autopilot log with mode, failsafe, battery and ESC telemetry for the end of the flight

data_requests.why_needed: Separates a commanded cut from a battery or power loss and from a propulsion hardware fault.

unobservable.fact: ESC and motor condition, and connector or wiring state on ch[2].
unobservable.why_it_matters: A propulsion hardware fault cannot be seen from commanded signals.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Inspect the ESC, motor and harness on ch[2] and run a bench spin test.

hypotheses.claim: The propulsion loop (throttle and ch[2]) lost its command or drive at 113.1 s.
hypotheses.because: Throttle went to 0 and ch[2] to minimum with correlation 0.995 between them. Nothing else shifted at that moment.
hypotheses.observed_at: commanded throttle and actuator output, not the motor itself

hypotheses.claim: A low battery or power cutoff caused the throttle to be cut.
hypotheses.because: A low-voltage warning appears at 1.057 s, but there are no battery signals near the cut.

hypotheses.claim: Roll and yaw instability before the cut led the controller or pilot to cut throttle.
hypotheses.because: The roll and yaw setpoints and attitude departed baseline before the cut, and roll tracking worsened (a7 at 103.475 s). Pitch and yaw tracking did not worsen after 113.1 s.

hypotheses.claim: An operator or autopilot failsafe commanded zero throttle.
hypotheses.because: The recording has no mode or failsafe signal, so it cannot show or exclude who commanded zero.

hypotheses.claim: The velocity step at 19.754 s was a state-estimator or sensor fault.
hypotheses.because: The 5 s medians return to normal flight values and setpoints changed at the same time, which looks like a manoeuvre.

events.why: Early in the flight and not shown to be linked to the cut, but the only event recorded.
